purpose: Isolate only the 220 QNM substitution in an already-used native waveform's post-attachment ringdown, then size it against existing whole-mode parity residuals.
method: Run the frozen historical-spline native 22 mode once per row and verify its exact array hashes against the campaign. On the same output chart reconstruct its ringdown from the returned remnant, boundary amplitude/phase/frequency/time, and published peak-preserving shape. Require historical reconstruction relative complex L2 <= 1e-12 over [boundary,boundary+100] M. Change only sigma to directly solved native 220 QNM divided by that same remnant mass fraction, preserving all preboundary samples and the original ringdown support rule.
metric_definitions: Postattachment complex and amplitude relative L2 use historical waveform norm in the denominator; phase is unwrap(angle(native * conj(historical))) over samples with historical amplitude >= 0.001 of the window peak, with RMS and maximum absolute. Full-mode complex relative L2 uses the original entire native chart. No realignment or refitting.
limitations: Two development rows only, not a domain-wide bound.
Comparison uses the native preattachment waveform and its fixed remnant/attachment, not an independently generated historical whole waveform.
The historical compatibility spline has black-box-inferred knot locations but was previously checked against the pinned LAL wheel at these remnant spins.
